approved: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill would declare a climate emergency in Australia.
All public service agencies would have to act in line with the declaration when making and carrying out policies, and report on their compliance each year.
A Multi-Party Climate Emergency Committee, including the Prime Minister and other party leaders, would be set up to guide the national response.
Declares an environment and climate emergency.
Requires public service agencies to follow the declaration and report annually on compliance.
Establishes a Multi-Party Climate Emergency Committee.
All public service agencies and their employees and agents.

The speaker seconded the Climate Emergency Declaration Bill 2020, arguing that Australia is in a climate emergency evidenced by devastating bushfires, and urged Parliament to declare an emergency and centre climate in policy decisions, citing 404,538 petition signatures, over 90 local councils, and the South Australian legislative assembly as supporting voices.
